description:
Redwood Inference will run a 6–8 week Vertical ABM pilot focused on regulated workloads, initially targeting 1–2 verticals (financial services and healthcare). The pilot’s goals are to (1) validate repeatable positioning + outbound motions for security- and compliance-driven buyers, (2) create a durable set of vertical assets (landing page, one-pagers, security FAQ/evidence pack, talk track, sequences), and (3) generate qualified pipeline for Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) with clear success criteria (meetings booked, SQLs created, pilots/POCs launched, and conversion to procurement).

Scope includes: building a target account list and persona map (CISO/Security, Platform/ML Engineering, Procurement), aligning messaging around latency/cost reliability plus compliance requirements (audit logs, SSO/SAML, retention/residency, KMS/HSM), launching targeted outreach (email + LinkedIn + partner channels), running discovery/demo/security reviews, and optionally executing 1–2 short technical pilots (benchmark + architecture validation) with solutions engineering. Out of scope: major new product features; only small documentation updates, packaging clarifications, and minor enablement work should be pulled in.

Key stakeholders: Camila Reyes (VP Marketing) and Ben Carter (Growth Marketing) drive campaign execution; Soojin Lee (Product Marketing) owns messaging/positioning; Stephanie Nguyen / Lukas Meyer and AEs (Avery Johnson, Priyom Das, Hannah Schmitt, Diego Fernandez) own account engagement and qualification; Markus Klein / SE team support technical deep dives; Naomi Feldman and Dr. Aisha Rahman provide security/compliance content and customer-facing responses; Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments) and Lauren Bishop (Dedicated) provide product alignment; Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes support contracting/procurement; Jasmine Liu / Rachel Kim plan CS handoff for any pilots that progress.

Timeline (example): Weeks 1–2 prep (account selection, messaging, assets, measurement); Weeks 3–6 execution (outreach + meetings + security reviews + pilots); Weeks 7–8 close (pipeline conversion, learnings, playbook, next-iteration plan). Constraints: compliance accuracy (no over-claiming), fast turnaround on security questionnaires, consistent packaging/pricing guidance, and tight feedback loops between Sales/PMM/Security/SE. Deliverables: vertical messaging frameworks, ABM landing page + one-pagers, security FAQ and evidence pack index, outbound sequences, webinar outline, sales enablement deck + battlecard, target account CRM hygiene, and a post-pilot readout with recommendations.

files.description: Published internal brief: pilot objectives, target vertical(s), ICP hypotheses, success metrics, governance (weekly cadence), and asset list; includes definitions for “regulated workload” and product mapping (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Messaging framework for financial services: personas (CISO, platform eng, risk), top pains, Redwood differentiators (audit logs, VPC/on-prem, predictable throughput), approved claims, objection handling, and sample talk tracks.

Messaging framework for healthcare/PHI-adjacent workloads: compliance requirements, deployment patterns, retention/residency considerations, and example use cases (member support, clinical summarization, coding assistance) with guardrails.

Sales-ready security FAQ for regulated buyers: SOC2/ISO posture, encryption/KMS, audit logging, RBAC/SSO/SAML, data retention/residency, incident response, and standard answers + links to evidence artifacts.
Enablement deck outline: problem framing, reference architectures (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), security posture, performance economics, sample pilot plan, and customer proof points (genericized).

Battlecard focused on regulated deployments: competitor positioning, common traps, differentiators (deployment flexibility + operational tooling), and recommended discovery questions to qualify for Private/Dedicated.

Index page describing what’s in the “evidence pack” for prospects (SOC2 report process, audit log samples, encryption diagrams, retention policy statements), how to request/share, and confidentiality guidance.

Internal packaging notes: typical Private/Dedicated commercial constructs for regulated customers (support tiers, compliance add-ons, retention controls), and guidance on when to involve Legal/Security.
Working doc with week-by-week plan, owners, deadlines, and a running risk log; includes meeting cadence and decision points (go/no-go for second vertical).
Spreadsheet-style table: target accounts, segment, region, known stack, intent signals, primary contacts, outreach status, and next action; includes scoring rubric for prioritization.
Notes on intent sources (website visits, benchmark downloads, partner referrals), how they map to lead scoring, and how Sales/Marketing will interpret signals during the pilot.
Matrix (often exported from a sheet) mapping personas to pains, proof points, assets, and CTAs; includes approved language vs “do not say” claims for compliance reasons.
Draft copy for regulated workloads landing page: headline options, sections, CTAs, security footnotes, and internal comments/edits from PMM/Security.
Customer-facing draft one-pager for finserv: architecture diagram (described), key security controls, pilot plan, and sample SLO targets; includes placeholders for customer logo/proof.
Customer-facing draft one-pager for healthcare: PHI-adjacent considerations, VPC/on-prem patterns, auditability, and example use cases; includes open questions for Legal/Compliance.
Outbound email sequence draft (3–5 touches): subject lines, personalization tokens, security-oriented CTA, and follow-up handling; notes on A/B variants.
Slides-like brief: target job titles, pain points, value props, creative direction, compliance review checklist, and measurement plan (CTR, form fills, meeting rate).
Outline for a webinar/virtual event: agenda, speakers, demo flow, security section, and audience Q&A prompts; includes promotion plan and follow-up email templates.
Spreadsheet-like metric definitions and tracking plan: target coverage, meetings, SQLs, POC starts, stage velocity, and qualitative signals; includes owner + data sources (HubSpot/Gmail).
Informal retro: what worked/failed in outreach, content gaps, security review bottlenecks, and recommended next iteration (vertical choice, partner motion, asset refresh).

CRM company record for a finserv target (Northbridge Banking): stage progression, notes from discovery/security review, deployment requirement (VPC/private), blockers, next step, and links to relevant calls/emails.
CRM record capturing payments use case (fraud ops + support), latency targets, model preferences, and key stakeholders; includes competitor mentions and planned demo dates.
CRM record emphasizing compliance and audit requirements; includes security questionnaire status, evidence requested, and procurement timeline assumptions.
Early-stage ABM account record: minimal context, intent signals, initial outbound attempts, and notes on org structure and potential champions.
Healthcare system target record: PHI-adjacent workloads, retention/residency needs, and pilot scoping notes; tracks multiple departments (IT security + app team).
Healthcare target record with on-prem constraints; highlights integration questions (networking, TLS, logging) and technical deep dive requirements.
Mid-market healthcare billing target: cost sensitivity, batch processing workloads, and evaluation plan; notes on Dedicated vs Hosted decision factors.
Wealth management target: strict audit logging + SSO requirements, internal governance; includes links to a technical deep dive and evidence pack requests.
Late-stage finserv target record: procurement/legal status, redline summary, required terms (DPA, SLA), and internal approval path.
Healthcare target record focused on patient support assistants; includes notes on data boundaries, retention controls, and outbound follow-up attempts.
Internal kickoff transcript: goals, vertical selection debate, asset owners, and timeline; captures open risks (security review bandwidth, proof points) and next steps.
Discovery call transcript with NorthBridge Bank: current stack, compliance constraints, success criteria, and next steps (security review + demo).
Demo transcript: Redwood Console, routing/fallback, Dedicated vs Private; includes Q&A on audit logging and regional isolation.
Security review transcript: SOC2 scope, encryption/KMS, retention policy, audit logs, SAML/SCIM; ends with a list of evidence items and deadlines.
POC scoping transcript: workload selection, evaluation dataset constraints, deployment topology (VPC), and responsibilities; includes risk around PHI handling.
Pilot check-in transcript: benchmark results, integration issues, logging requirements, and action items for Redwood SE + customer platform team.
Pilot check-in transcript: progress vs success criteria, security team feedback, and early procurement signals; includes next meeting scheduling.
Technical deep dive transcript: audit log fields, export patterns, KMS/HSM integration, and operational considerations for regulated environments.
Procurement/legal call transcript: DPA, SLA language, data residency, liability caps; includes follow-ups requiring counsel review.
Partner/process call transcript: AWS Marketplace private offer workflow, compliance positioning, and how to align ABM targets with partner co-sell.
Closeout transcript: recap results, confirm success criteria, discuss rollout plan, and define CS handoff artifacts (runbooks, SLO monitoring).
Closeout transcript: decision on Dedicated vs Private, remaining security gaps, and next-step plan for procurement and implementation timeline.
